| [NOTE-005](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-005.md) v2 | Spectral dimensions of bundled networks | The paper studies a "bundled" network, meaning a fiber graph attached at one node to every node of a base graph, with base and fiber growing with the same length L. For such a network, first-order perturbation theory (SM Eq. 10) gives the low spectrum as λ = ℓ^b/N_f, and from that the gap ("Fiedler") dimension d_g = 2(d_f,f + d_f,b)/(d_f,f + 2d_f,b/d_g,b), while the spectral dimension stays d_s = d_s,f. The two therefore differ unless d_g,b = 2 or the fiber is finite. For example, the ring-of-rings comb has d_s = 1 but d_g = 4/3, and the 2D-base brush has d_s = 1 but d_g = 2. | [NOTE-567](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-567.md) | Network Epistemology: Communication in Epistemic Communities | A survey. At r = 2 the greedy rule (pass to the contact nearest the target in lattice distance) delivers in O((log n)²) expected steps (proved for p = q = 1); for 0 ≤ r < 2 every such algorithm needs Ω(n^((2−r)/3)) and for r > 2 Ω(n^((r−2)/(r−1))). So efficient decentralized search depends on how the long-range links are distributed relative to the lattice, not on the links' existence or on the graph's diameter. The consensus is then a linear opinion pool whose weights are the chain's stationary vector, which gives members outside the closed class no weight. Two closed classes, or one periodic class, give no consensus. The weights are fixed, and nothing in the model tracks the truth. | Read |

| [NOTE-1218](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1218.md) | Torres-Hugas et al. — Cycle holonomy and remote synchronization | For a phase model whose edges carry antisymmetric phase lags, the twisted Laplacian Lα = δα*δα has a zero mode exactly when every cycle holonomy is 0 mod 2π, and otherwise its smallest eigenvalue measures the residual incompatibility; for an isolated ℓ-cycle that eigenvalue is largest at holonomy π. | [NOTE-1224](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1224.md) | Singer — Angular synchronization | Angles θ₁, …, θₙ are estimated, up to one global phase, from noisy offsets θᵢ − θⱼ of which an unknown fraction are pure outliers, by the top eigenvector of the Hermitian matrix Hᵢⱼ = e^{iδᵢⱼ} or by an SDP like Goemans–Williamson's. On the complete graph a random-matrix argument puts the eigenvector's threshold at p > 1/√n good offsets, with the expected squared correlation near 1/(1 + 1/(np²)). Kron reduction fails for general sheaves, because an interior vertex can impose constraints on the boundary that no pairwise sheaf expresses. It scores a candidate by the derivative of a proxy utility of the transport plan (how near a permutation, or how consistent with the graphs, the plan is) with respect to supervising each possible match, averaged over matches by the current plan. The derivative is exact, from one singular positive semidefinite linear system solved by conjugate gradients. At a fixed budget of 20% extra labels on top of 20% given, it beats uncertainty baselines by up to 2.8 MRR points and random choice by up to 16, without variances reported. | Read |
| [NOTE-1328](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1328.md) | Vayer et al. — Fused Gromov–Wasserstein | FGW compares two attributed graphs with one coupling whose cost mixes, with weight α, a Wasserstein term on node features and a Gromov–Wasserstein term on structure. For α in (0, 1), q = 1 and distance-matrix structures it is a metric that vanishes exactly when a bijection preserves weights, features and structure. As α tends to 0 or 1 it tends to W or GW. On benchmark graph classification it is competitive with graph kernels, but the supplement shows Wasserstein on features alone matching or beating it on several datasets. | Read |
| [NOTE-1330](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1330.md) | Chowdhury & Mémoli — Network Gromov–Wasserstein | The Gromov–Wasserstein distance, defined by minimizing the distortion of a coupling, is a pseudometric on all measure networks: any Polish node set with a probability measure and any bounded, possibly asymmetric, edge-weight function. It is zero exactly when the two networks are weakly isomorphic, that is, when both are images of one network that preserves weights and measures. Cheap invariants give a hierarchy of lower bounds, and the third lower bound, a transport problem whose costs are themselves transport problems, reduces to one-dimensional transport in closed form. The bounds are one-sided: networks can agree on every invariant and still be apart. | Read |
| [NOTE-1331](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1331.md) | Sarkar, Mukherjee and Sato — Attention as lattice gauge theory | Under per-entity O(d) frame freedom, transports carry invariant information only around cycles, a triangle's invariants are class functions of its holonomy, and an equivariant edge update is Ψ(H)Tᵢⱼ with Ψ conjugation-equivariant: a sound conditional theorem, standard in lattice gauge theory and synchronization, whose "unique form" is a family. The untrained S4 experiments show composition doing the work and Wilson-loop routing adding 0.6–7.8 points; the 0.99 AUC is a ceiling the data's construction sets, as the paper itself computes. | Read |
| [NOTE-1332](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1332.md) | Bodnar et al. — Neural sheaf diffusion | Bodnar et al. read sheaf diffusion on a graph as a projection onto the harmonic space of a sheaf Laplacian and ask which classes of restriction maps can make that projection linearly separate a node labelling. A symmetric one-dimensional sheaf, which is a weighted graph Laplacian, cannot separate the two sides of a balanced bipartite graph; signed maps separate any two classes; no one-dimensional sheaf separates three; diagonal maps with d ≥ C stalks, and O(d) bundles for C ≤ 2d at d = 2 and 4, separate any number. Every one of these sheaves is built from the labels. Learned from features, such sheaves give competitive node classification on six small heterophilic benchmarks. The claim that the O(d) construction exists only at d = 2 and 4 is wrong: it works at d = 8 too. | Read |
| [NOTE-1334](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1334.md) | Zeng et al. — HOT multi-network alignment | Aligns K networks at once by one multi-marginal coupling tensor. The networks are first co-clustered through a fused Gromov–Wasserstein barycenter, then each cluster's nodes are aligned by multi-marginal fused GW with a cost from anchor-based random-walk embeddings, solved by a KL proximal point method. The joint objective at any tensor is the sum of the pairwise objectives at its marginals, so it bounds the sum of pairwise optima from above. On three-network benchmarks whose true correspondences are consistent by construction, it beats pairwise and multi-network baselines in pairwise and high-order hits; no experiment isolates the joint coupling from the new cost and the clustering. | Read |
| [NOTE-1354](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1354.md) v2 | Škorić, de Hoogh and Zannone — Evidence-based subjective logic | Subjective logic's discounting x ⊗ y multiplies opinions and does not distribute over its evidence-adding consensus ⊕, so trust networks must be put in a canonical form, often by discarding edges, to avoid double-counting. EBSL replaces it with x ⊡ y = g(x)·y, a scalar multiple of y's evidence, which distributes over ⊕; the recursive, PageRank-like fixed point R = A ⊕ (offdiag R ⊡ A) then handles loops without discarding anything, and on Tribler data it converges in 9–47 iterations. There is no ground truth; robustness to self-promotion, slander and Sybil attacks is left for future work. | Read |
| [NOTE-1356](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1356.md) | Castro and Liskov — Practical Byzantine fault tolerance | A state-machine replication protocol that keeps safety with at most ⌊(n − 1)/3⌋ arbitrarily faulty replicas and no timing assumption, needing weak synchrony only for liveness; a three-phase commit within views and a view change that carries prepared requests forward. With MACs in place of signatures, a replicated NFS ran the Andrew benchmark 3% slower than Digital Unix's NFS on four replicas, with view changes not yet implemented in the measured library. | Read |
| [NOTE-1374](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1374.md) | Friedkin — A formal theory of reflected appraisals in the evolution of power | Friedkin extends the Friedkin–Johnsen influence model across a sequence of issues: each member's self-weight on the next issue is set to their average total control over the last. In 50 four-person laboratory groups, prior control predicts the next self-weight. In 100,000 simulated random networks, over 98% evolve to one leader whose uninfluenced preference settles every issue through intermediaries. A re-run reproduces this, and shows that the DeGroot–Friedkin version of [LIT-1146](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1146.md) does not concentrate power on the same networks. | Read |
| [NOTE-1381](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1381.md) | Halpern and Moses — Knowledge and common knowledge in a distributed environment | Defines distributed, someone-, everyone- and common knowledge for processors in a system of runs, and shows that a guaranteed coordinated attack makes the attack common knowledge (Proposition 4), while over a channel that may lose any message nothing becomes common knowledge that would not be common knowledge with no messages delivered (Theorem 5), so no correct protocol ever attacks (Corollary 6). Temporal imprecision alone, uncertain start times and delivery times, makes common knowledge unattainable (Theorem 8). Weaker fixed-point variants (ε-, eventual and timestamped common knowledge) are attainable in many systems. | Read |
| [NOTE-1385](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1385.md) | Holme and Newman — Coevolution of networks and opinions | N agents with G = N/γ possible opinions on a random graph; at each step a random agent either moves one of its edges to a random holder of its own opinion (probability φ) or copies a random neighbour's opinion (1 − φ). The process always ends in disconnected communities each of one opinion. For k̄ = 4 and γ = 10 a continuous transition at φ_c = 0.458 ± 0.008 separates a giant like-minded community plus small ones (φ < φ_c) from only small communities of mean size about γ (φ > φ_c), with exponents a = 0.61, b = 0.7 and z = 0.61 outside the percolation class. Simulation only. | Read |
| [NOTE-1392](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1392.md) | DeMarzo, Vayanos and Zwiebel — Persuasion bias, social influence, and unidimensional opinions | Agents average the reports of those they listen to with fixed relative weights, treating every round's report as new (persuasion bias, a DeGroot model). In a strongly connected network they reach a consensus weighted by the stationary distribution of the listening matrix, so influence comes from network position as well as precision; the consensus is correct only in "balanced" networks, and fully rational agents who know the network reach the correct beliefs in at most N² rounds. Long-run differences of opinion line up along one line given by the second eigenvectors, across every issue. | Read |
| [NOTE-1394](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1394.md) v2 | Gross and Blasius — Adaptive coevolutionary networks | Reviews models, mostly 1998–2007, in which a network's topology and its nodes' states change each other, and names four recurrent outcomes: robust self-organization toward critical states (Bornholdt and Rohlf's threshold networks reach K = 2), spontaneous "division of labour" into classes of nodes (Ito and Kaneko), complex topologies from local rules, and new system-level dynamics such as bistability and oscillation in an adaptive SIS epidemic. A sketch, not a theory: the mechanisms are argued from examples, and its summary of Holme and Newman inverts the model's parameter. | Read |
| [NOTE-1403](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1403.md) | Kleinman, Liu and Redding — International friends and enemies | A country's real-income elasticity to a partner's productivity, from a constant-elasticity trade model with input-output links, predicts political alignment with that partner. Instrumented by a counterfactual Chinese productivity shock from the 1980 equilibrium (119 countries, 1980–2010) or by air-versus-sea distance (pairs, 1970–2012), it moves UN voting similarity (0.094 SD per SD in the panel), lowers strategic rivalry, and raises formal alliances. The paper's own model is strategic: alignment is a costly action a country takes to raise a partner on whom its income depends. | Read |
| [NOTE-1410](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1410.md) | Akkoyunlu, Ekanadham and Huber — Some constraints and tradeoffs in the design of network communications | A design paper on interprocess communication in networks of sequential processes: complete status of a transaction is impossible in an arbitrary distributed facility and, with time-outs, even in a reliable one, and the insertion property forces the system to withhold status. Its Appendix states, as a story of gangsters and a messenger who may be mugged, that no finite exchange over a lossy channel brings two parties to know they agree a message got through, with a shortest-sequence proof. That is the coordinated attack problem in substance, three years before Gray (1978), framed as mutual knowledge of delivery. | Read |
| [NOTE-1414](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1414.md) | Ito and Kaneko — Spontaneous structure formation in a network of chaotic units | In a globally coupled logistic map whose units each renormalize their incoming weights after strengthening those from units in similar states, identical units split, in the desynchronized high-turnover regime, into a persistent core that the others attend to and a periphery the core ignores; the split needs states and weights to act on each other. Simulation only, N = 100, one parameter point in detail. | Read |
